title: For my daughter Nasreen on her wedding day
titleOriginal: اپنی بیٹی نسرین اختر دی رخصتی تے شعری نذرانہ
takeaway: A father's advice to his daughter as she leaves home: be kind, be brave, and never forget God.
scene: In South Asian weddings, the 'rukhsati' is the emotional moment when the bride leaves her parents' home for her husband's. Here the poet gives his daughter Nasreen Akhtar a poem as a gift: part blessing, part advice for her new life.
context: Traditional advice. This is how many fathers of the poet's generation spoke to a daughter on her wedding day. Some of it is timeless, like kindness and patience. Some of it reflects family expectations of that time.

original: جگ اندر خشی سدا نال وسیں پالے ویر بھیناں سبھے کہندیاں نیں
چنبا چڑیاں دا دانے کہن سارے دھیاں سدا نہ پیکڑے رہندیاں نیں
transliteration: Jag andar khushi sada naal vaseen, paale veer bhainaan sabbhe kehndiyaan nain
Chamba chiriyaan da daane kehn saare, dhiyaan sada na pekre rehndiyaan nain
translation: 'May you always live happily in the world,' say all the brothers and sisters who grew up with you.
Wise people say daughters are a flock of sparrows: they don't stay in their parents' home forever.
couplets.story: All her brothers and sisters wish her a happy life. Then an old Punjabi saying: daughters are like a flock of little birds. They don't stay in their parents' nest forever. One day they fly off to start their own homes.

original: سدا سنگ سہیلیاں نئیں رہنا نہ ای خشی دیاں ندیاں وہندیاں نیں
خشی نال اوہ سوہریاں گھر وسن مٹھے بول جو مونہہ تھیں کہندیاں نیں
transliteration: Sada sang saheliyaan nahin rehna, na ee khushi diyaan nadiyaan vehndiyaan nain
Khushi naal oh sauhriyaan ghar vasan, mitthe bol jo moonh thin kehndiyaan nain
translation: You won't always be with your girlfriends, and rivers of happiness don't always flow.
The brides who live happily in their in-laws' homes are the ones who speak sweet words.
couplets.story: She won't always have her friends around her, and life isn't always happy. But brides who speak kindly in their new home are the ones who live happily there.

original: گھر سارا ای جنت نظر ہوندا شرماں والیاں جس تھاں جو رہندیاں نیں
اوہ سدا ای ٹھنڈیاں چھاواں مانن سس سوہرے دی منت رہندیاں نیں
transliteration: Ghar saara ee jannat nazar honda, sharmaan vaaliyaan jis thaan jo rehndiyaan nain
Oh sada ee thandiyaan chhaavaan maanan, sass sohre di mannat rehndiyaan nain
translation: A whole house looks like paradise wherever modest, well-mannered women live.
They always enjoy cool shade, those who stay respectful to their mother-in-law and father-in-law.
couplets.story: A home feels like paradise when the women in it are gentle and well-mannered. A bride who respects her husband's parents will always find a cool, safe 'shade' in that home.

original: وانگ پھلاں دی باس دے سدا مہکن گھل مل جو جیہیاں وچ رہندیاں نیں
دیور جیٹھ نناں دی کرے عزت چھاں سکھاں دی ہیٹھ اوہ بہندیاں نیں
transliteration: Vaang phullaan di baas de sada mehkan, ghul mil jo jiyaan vich rehndiyaan nain
Devar jeth nanaan di kare izzat, chhaan sukhaan di heth oh behndiyaan nain
translation: Like the scent of flowers, they always give off fragrance, those who mix in warmly with everyone.
Whoever respects her husband's younger and elder brothers and his sisters sits in the shade of comfort.
couplets.story: Brides who get along warmly with everyone are like the smell of flowers, making the whole house lovely. If she respects all her husband's brothers and sisters, she'll live comfortably and happily.

original: غافل رب رسول توں نہ رہنا نیک جداں دے بول اوہ سہندیاں نیں
احمدؔ وانگ توں جرات تھیں رہیں ہر دم آہری نال نہ اوکڑاں کھہندیاں نیں
transliteration: Ghaafil Rab Rasool ton na rehna, nek jidaan de bol oh sehndiyaan nain
Ahmad vaang toon jur'at thin raheen har dam, aahri naal na aukraan khehndiyaan nain
translation: Never be careless about God and His Messenger; good women bear even harsh words patiently.
Like Ahmad, always live with courage: hardships don't beat those who keep working hard.
couplets.story: His most important advice comes last. Never forget God and the Prophet. Good people stay patient even when others say hurtful things. And be brave, like your father: problems can't beat someone who keeps working hard.

deeper: The poem's centre is its final advice: 'Never be careless about God and His Messenger.' The other virtues, sweet speech, patience, respect for elders and hard work, are presented as part of that faith, lived out in daily family life.
why: A father's farewell to his daughter on her wedding day. The advice reflects the traditional values of the time, and the love behind it is easy to see.
